mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 5.25% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary stance, which raises discount rates and depresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when this trigger is met, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a rise in the unemployment rate above 4% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly below zero at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase of at least 0.4 percentage points in the unemployment rate for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which erode consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises by >= 0.4pp for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative in at least 70% of triggered periods, or the median return is not below the 5th percentile of the historical distribution.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline of more than 1% in the industrial production index (INDPRO) while the unemployment rate is below 4% indicates supply-side contraction in a tight labor market, which raises input costs and reduces profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: tight labor market with supply shock
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not statistically distinguishable from zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase of at least 2% in real retail sales (proxied by RSAFS) over three consecutive months signals robust consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS rises by >= 2% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive in at least 60% of triggered periods, or the median return is below the 50th percentile of the historical distribution.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp reduction in the federal funds rate below 3% during a period when the unemployment rate exceeds 5% signals an emergency monetary easing in response to severe economic distress, which initially boosts risk assets and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive in at least 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is below the 25th percentile of the historical distribution.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the unemployment rate below 3.5% for four consecutive months signals a tightening labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as profit margins compress.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative in at least 60% of triggered periods, or the median return is above the historical median.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent quarterly decline in GDP (GDPC1) for two consecutive quarters signals a macroeconomic recession, which reduces corporate earnings and increases downside risk, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 declines for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative in at least 70% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not below the 25th percentile of the historical distribution.
